comment: Outlets whose public RSS/Atom feeds fill the weird-news front page (/api/weird, lib/weird.js). As with the brief (data/news-sources.json) we show only the outlet's own headline, its name, the time, a link to the story and the outlet's own link-preview image: never its description, opening paragraph or article text. Every item passes the moderation rules in lib/moderation.js first. Feed addresses come from the scout's research (the build sandbox could not reach any of them); the lead checked them on a Vercel preview with /api/weird?debug=1 on 16 Nov 2026 (results in each entry's 'checked' note). The owner should review and approve this list before launch. Guardian and NPR are left out on purpose: their feed terms are personal, non-commercial use only.
fields: name: shown as the outlet. section: the outlet's section the feed covers. home: the outlet's page we link to (also its own-site boundary for og:image reads). enabled: false = the feed is still read for ?debug=1 but none of its stories is used. stale: the date its feed was last seen with nothing from the past 14 days (kept: it may post again). images: false = no picture is read or shown, and its article pages are never fetched. review: true = a higher-risk outlet; its items appear only if moderation passes, never above a regular outlet's item, at most 3 at a time. minWeirdness: the lowest weirdness() score (lib/weird.js) a story needs to run; 0 for an odd-news desk, 1 for an outlet's own offbeat section, 2 for a general feed. cap: at most this many of its stories at once (default 8, 3 for review outlets). listicles: false = drop listicles, quizzes and evergreen explainers. categoryHints: lower-case words found in the feed's own <category> labels -> our category. filter: when present, an item is kept only if one of its feed categories contains one of 'categories' or its URL path contains one of 'paths'. exclude: an item is dropped when its headline contains one of 'titles' (whole words, any case) or its URL path one of 'paths'. licence: what we know about the terms.

sources.name: UPI
sources.licence: Unknown: no feed reuse terms found (upi.com footer Terms of Use not read). Preview photos are often Reuters/AP/Getty wire photos: keep the images switch and takedown route ready.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 25 items, 20 kept

sources.name: Sky News
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, but all 4 items older than 14 days. Kept in case it posts again

sources.name: Smithsonian Magazine
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 268 items, 41 kept before the weirdness minimum: mostly ordinary science and culture, hence minWeirdness 2 and cap 3

sources.name: Atlas Obscura
sources.licence: Unknown (terms page found, not read in full). Prefer /feeds/articles over /feeds/latest, which is mostly user-submitted places.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 18 items, 3 kept

sources.name: ScienceDaily
sources.licence: Known: feeds free for commercial and non-commercial use with ScienceDaily credited as the source (terms dated 7 Jan 2026); the outlet name is shown on every item. The terms count 'altering content or failing to display it' as a breach: ask ScienceDaily whether headline-and-link complies before launch. Images off: they are usually credited to the releasing institution.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 60 items, 26 kept

sources.name: Mental Floss
sources.licence: Unknown (mentalfloss.com/terms-of-use not read). Shopping posts, listicles, quizzes and evergreen explainers are filtered out.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 75 items, 65 kept before the listicle filter and weirdness minimum (it flooded the page with evergreen lists and quizzes)

sources.name: Live Science
sources.licence: Unknown (Future plc terms not read). General feed, filtered to these sections and then to stories with a weirdness signal. Runs graphic medical case reports: the injury and health rule holds those.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 50 items, all 50 dropped by the first filter (strange-news labels only). Filter widened to the feed's section labels; /api/weird?debug=1 now lists the labels each feed uses

sources.name: SoraNews24
sources.licence: Unknown (no terms page found). General feed: only stories with a weirdness signal run (a 'weird' label from the outlet counts); crime and sexual content are held or dropped by moderation.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, 20 items, 2 kept (18 dropped by the old 'weird' category filter, now replaced by the weirdness minimum)

sources.name: Oddity Central
sources.licence: Unknown (no terms page found). High risk: rewrites other outlets' stories and runs viral private individuals, medical conditions and poverty. Images off; lower priority; review outlet.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: ok on the Vercel preview, but all 10 items older than 14 days. Kept in case it posts again

sources.name: NDTV
sources.licence: Unknown (footer terms not read). High risk: heavy on viral clips of private people and accidents. Images off; lower priority; review outlet.
sources.checked: 2026-11-16: the old address (feeds.feedburner.com/ndtvnews-offbeat) answered 200 but was not a feed. This address (…/ndtvnews-offbeat-news) is the one a third-party RSS reader lists for NDTV Offbeat; it is not confirmed by NDTV. Disabled until /api/weird?debug=1 shows it ok, then set enabled to true
